_comment: Maps a requirement id (as the HOST reports it in GetHostState) to the yak package that
installs it. This is the missing link between 'what is declared' and 'what to actually
run': the 210 requirements say what a machine needs, and this says how to get it.
GROUNDED column: 'capture' means the id was read from a live GetHostState on the dev
machine (workloads/rhino/results/environment.json) - it is what the host really calls
the thing. 'inferred' means the id has NOT been observed loaded anywhere, and the
package name is a reasonable guess from the filename. An inferred id must be confirmed
against a real capture before anything depends on it: a requirement whose id never
matches is a guard that can never fire, which is how bug 0022 happened.
Package files live in the yak source folder, declared as %CANARY_HANDOFF%/_yak so a
machine with the Drive mounted elsewhere can repoint it by setting CANARY_HANDOFF.
Names here are the package NAME, not the filename - yak resolves the version itself.

note: NOT OBSERVED LOADED ANYWHERE. The dev machine's capture contains zero occurrences
of 'penumbra' in its loaded list - no rhino: id and no gh: id - yet 62 rhino tests
hard-depend on the Penumbra Rhino plug-in through the WaitForPenumbraFrame action.
So either those tests do not pass today, or the plug-in reaches Rhino by a route
PlugIn.GetInstalledPlugIns() does not report. The id below is a GUESS from the
assembly name and MUST be replaced with whatever a real capture shows before any
test declares it. Installing this package is still safe; declaring the id is not.
